Topic:AFL Women’s

Wed 15 Jul 2026 at 1:00pm

AFLW games are played at suburban and boutique stadiums. (Getty: Mark Kolbe)

The AFLW is about to enter its 11th season, and over that time, one issue has remained a constant bugbear for players, coaches and fans: where games are played.

The AFL is steadfast on using suburban and boutique stadiums for games, including for marquee games and the grand final, despite calls from the wider women's football community for bigger venues.

Last season, the AFL responded to concerns about the standard of venues used in the AFLW competition by consolidating the number of locations.

However, a significant gap remains between the big stadiums and lower-tier facilities.

Weather conditions can impact the quality of the game. (Getty: James Wiltshire/AFL Photos)

AFL Players Association CEO James Gallagher said on behalf of the players, the union would continue to advocate for better venues for AFLW games, as it believed this was in the best interests of the competition.

"AFLW games are played at many venues which vary in quality of facilities, surface, capacity, access and weather-proofing. This impacts the experience and product for players and fans, as well as player safety," Gallagher told ABC Sport.

"Games in the best possible conditions showcase the skill and talent of our members, elevate the AFLW competition, and lead to a better broadcast product and fan experience."

AFLW burst onto the scene nine years ago with a lockout crowd but since then, crowds have dwindled. Here's how the league plans to get them back up.

This season, however, the league has introduced four double-headers, with women's games to be played at tier-one venues. Gallagher said this was a step in the right direction.

Data from the AFL Players Association in its Insights and Impacts Report found that of the 28 venues used across Australia for AFLW games last year, players rated 11 of them average or below for surface quality and facilities. These venues hosted 31 per cent of all games.

Only three venues were rated "very good" by players for surface and facilities: Carrara Oval (Queensland), Springfield Central Stadium (Queensland) and Kardinia Park (Victoria). These are all venues also used for AFL men's matches or as club training facilities.

Officials and players have raised safety concerns about some grounds, including Collingwood's home ground of Victoria Park.

In 2024, a burst water pipe flooded an area of the turf before the game, requiring ground staff to drain it and pack it with a mixture of sand and sawdust, and in 2025, sand was reportedly painted green to look like turf.

In the Insights and Impacts Report, players noted that stadiums also had an impact on fan experience, broadcast quality, fixture equity and audience reach.

Lighting quality for night matches influences which venues receive prime-time slots. This means that some games between top eight teams are not played in the best time slots.

Sand was used to cover a hole in the ground due to a leak in an underground water pipe moments before an AFLW game. (Getty: Dylan Burns/AFL Photos)

The last three AFLW grand finals at Princes Park sold out, prompting calls from fans and the wider women's football community to move the event to a larger stadium to meet growing demand.

However, Docklands Stadium just down the road, which is owned by the AFL and has a capacity of more than 53,000, is not in contention to be utilisied as the league remains steadfast it will not host standalone games there until there is proof of sufficient demand.

The upcoming Australia v Ireland AFLW game ahead of the season is scheduled at North Sydney Oval, despite selling out and calls to move it to the Sydney Cricket Ground (SCG).

The AFL hopes the introduction of double-headers will increase exposure to the women's game among existing men's football fans, while addressing some of the challenges of smaller venues.

The double-headers include two at Docklands Stadium, including the season opener between Carlton and St Kilda for Spud's Round, one at Sydney Showgrounds Stadium and one at the SCG.

There is a signficant difference in quality between the best and worst stadiums used for AFLW games. (Getty: Josh Chadwick/AFL Photos)

After Essendon and Hawthorn played their inaugural AFLW clash at Docklands Stadium in 2022 in front of a 12,000-strong crowd, the coaches called for more games to be played at the venue.

"We saw both teams put on a really great show tonight, so why not play more games at big stadiums?" Hawks then-coach Bec Goddard said. "It felt like there were so many more than 12,000 here tonight. That's a big number, but it sounded a lot louder.

"Just give the women the opportunity to play in big stadiums, and the fans will come."

Players rate a large portion of grounds used for AFLW games average or below average. (Getty: James Wiltshire/AFL Photos)

AFLW star Tilly Lucas-Rodd agreed, saying that being sheltered from the elements made for a better spectacle.

"There were no conditions … I think you saw that. The skills were up because there weren't any other factors," Lucas-Rodd said.

However, no games have been played at Docklands since then and the upcoming double-header in August.
